stations.name: Punta Arenas Magallanes
stations.from: PUNTA ARENAS MAGALLANES, CHILE. Servicio Meteorologico de la Armada de Chile. From "Worldwide Marine Radiofacsimile Broadcast Schedules" (NOAA, edition of March 7, 2025); information dated Sep 23, 2010. The source prints the schedules of Valparaiso and Punta Arenas together and the reader may have put a row under the wrong station: the rows from 1100 to 0405 are taken as Valparaiso's and those from 1115 to 2325 as Punta Arenas'. All 120/576, 1 kW. The source says the Antarctic ice limit charts are no longer sent by radiofacsimile. Position: the city of the station name, to a tenth of a degree; the source does not give the transmitter site.

stations.from: SEOUL, REPUBLIC OF KOREA. Korea Meteorological Administration. From "Worldwide Marine Radiofacsimile Broadcast Schedules" (NOAA, edition of March 7, 2025); information dated Jan 01, 2009: "Many of these reports may be in Korean". All 120/576, 3 kW. A row with two times is sent at both; ---- = not sent. The source has a row at 0047/1247 with no title: not included. Notes of the source: 300 Hz black and white signal for 10 s before phasing, phasing 30 s, stop 15 s; "tsunami warning" is transmitted without delay. Position: the city of the station name, to a tenth of a degree; the source does not give the transmitter site.

stations.name: Pevek
stations.from: PEVEK, CHUKOTKA PENINSULA, RUSSIA. DOUBTFUL STATION: the information in "Worldwide Marine Radiofacsimile Broadcast Schedules" (NOAA, edition of March 7, 2025) is dated 11/97 and nothing newer confirms it is on the air. Long wave (148 kHz), ice charts at 90 lines per minute, index 576. Each broadcast is given as a two-hour window (0530-0730, 1130-1330, 1430-1630): the time here is the start of the window. No call sign and no power in the source. Position: the city of the station name, to a tenth of a degree; the source does not give the transmitter site.

stations.from: MURMANSK, RUSSIA. DOUBTFUL STATION. Schedule from "Worldwide Marine Radiofacsimile Broadcast Schedules" (NOAA, edition of March 7, 2025), which warns that the schedule "may no longer be transmitted on-air" and whose frequencies (5336, 6445.5, 7908.8, 10130 kHz) are old. Frequencies used here: 6328.5 and 8444 kHz, the ones the DX Info Centre list (W. R. Hepburn, 2025-03-17) gives as active or reported active, with the same times on the air as this schedule.
